macro.narrative: The US economy is running hot on the real side (May payrolls +172k vs 80k expected, unemployment 4.3%, Q2 GDP tracking ~3%) but is absorbing a supply-side inflation shock from the Iran conflict and the effectively-closed Strait of Hormuz, which pushed Brent from ~$95 to a $138 April peak and drove headline CPI to 3.8% (core 2.8%). With cuts off the table and markets now pricing a 37-45% chance of a Fed HIKE under new Chair Warsh, the 10y sits at 4.55% and the 30y above 5%, tightening financial conditions into equities trading at a CAPE of 42.5 and a near-zero equity risk premium. This is a stagflation-lite regime where solid nominal growth masks a fragile risk-asset setup: any further energy escalation is directly inflationary and hawkish, while a signed ceasefire is the main bullish catalyst. We tilt modestly defensive — favoring real assets (commodities/gold), cash, and the USD over richly-priced equities and tight credit — but stop short of full risk-off given the absence of recession or credit stress.
